rules_text:
Rules summary Contents 1 Basic info 1.1 Card ranking 2 Hand 2.1 Calculating points 3 Between hands and rounds 4 Game end Basic info Mate is a 2 player game of perfect information played with 20 standard cards: the 7 , 10 , Q , K and A of each suit. A match is made of 2 rounds , and each round is made of 2 hands (total of 4 hands). Card ranking Mate is a trick-taking game, so cards and suits are ranked to determine the trick winner, as follows: A > 10 > K > Q > 7 ( A strongest, 7 weakest); Clubs > spades > hearts > diamonds ( clubs strongest, diamonds weakest). Hand When the first hand starts, the deck is shuffled and 10 cards are dealt to each player. That means all cards are dealt and players know their opponent's hand . Then, up to 10 tricks are played, following these steps: The first player plays any card from their hand; The second one plays other card of the same suit , if possible. If they don't have a card of the current suit, they may play a card of other suit, but of the same value of the first card; Whoever played the strongest card wins the trick and starts the next one. If the second player doesn't have any playable card (no card of the current suit or value), that's a mate . The hand is finished and the first player of the trick (who forced the mate) scores ! If all tricks are played without a mate, it's a tie and nobody scores . Calculating points Points are calculated according to the card used to force the mate and the number of tricks played in the hand (including the current one). The weight of the card is multiplied by the number of tricks ( weight x tricks = points ). The longer you take a hand before a mate, the better. Weights : A -> 11 ; 10 -> 10 ; 7 -> 7 ; K -> 4 ; Q -> 3 . For instance, if a player forces a mate with a K in the 7th trick , they score 28 points . Between hands and rounds After the first hand of the first round, the deck is NOT shuffled : players exchange all their cards and a new hand starts. This removes luck from the game. After the second hand of the first round, the deck is shuffled , cards are dealt and the second (and last) round starts. It's played exactly as the first one , with 2 hands. Game end The game ends when the second round is finished. The player with more points wins .

[Rating: 3/10] A 2p OG trick taking game where all players know exactly what other players have and hands are swapped to eliminate luck. Players will play a card and either play the same card of different suit or same suit of different value, with the higher value then suit winning the trick. Each game consists of 2 rounds, 2 hands each. A hand ends once a player can not play a card, which hands out points based on number of turns and card played to win. Most points wins. This game isn't for me, best for those who like to card count and 0 luck in their games.

[Rating: 3.5/10] More like an interesting puzzle to try to try to solve than an actual game that is fun.

[Rating: 4/10] The spaces of a 4x5 grid are randomly divided between the players, who then alternately expend them with the goal of leaving the opponent without a valid response. Various niggles: 1) The scoring multipliers of the columns seem a bit arbitrary. 2) The "foreplacing" mechanism is an embellishment that detracts from the game's main focus. 3) If you play with cards on hand instead of on the table, it unnecessarily obscures the game state. 4) Playing each setup twice isn't entirely fair since the second player knows the outcome of the first round when starting the second.

[Rating: 5/10] Pretty cool card game.  Haven't played enough to really get a feel for the deep strategy.  But how can you go wrong with chess and cards?

[Rating: 5/10] It was cool to play a card game invented in Germany in 1915. I could just imagine some guy in the dirty trenches, finding ways to kill some time. Anyway, this is a sure brain burner! It's a bit overwhelming to have a perfect information game where each player has an equal chance of beating the other. For what should be a light card game, I spent a minute or so on each move, which made things slow. Still, interesting idea and good to know the rules when there is only a deck of cards around. Jen gets a value 11 score, which is the difference between our two scores.

[Rating: 5/10] Brought to this gem by Sid Sackson. Clever designed old school strategic micro game for 2p. Unfortunately only fun when using card memorizing. So the perfect game to learn and enjoy card counting.

[Rating: 5/10] Perfect information trick taking for two. Switch hand for second half of the round.

[Rating: 6/10] A very interesting card game. It felt like if I spent 10 minutes thinking things through I could come up with the "perfect" play. But that sucks the fun out of a 2p game if you sit around for 10 minutes thinking before playing. So while I admire the structure of the game and its "mirror play" at it felt too dry for me.

[Rating: 6/10] Very original, excitant and clever game. It´s one of my favourites from A Gamut of games. I´m not sure if I prefer it with the original rules or the Lovet's 'chess cards' variant. The former desarves a bit of bluffing with the hidden foreplaced card, and the second is a fully open information one. The second player in each round, after the swap has some advantage, so you must play two rounds to balance it.
